- When sentiment is strongly negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or adjust downward by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is positive but recent price action is flat or declining, model overestimates upside — reduce forecast slope or apply mild downward drag (e.g., -0.5 to -1.0% per day).
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 30-day moving average, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast momentum toward average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward volatility in negative sentiment periods — add 0.5–1.0% buffer below forecast if sentiment < -0.2 for 3+ days.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more) in last 5 days, model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values or apply 0.5% dampening factor.
